attractions.name: Shrine of Shah Rukn-e-Alam
attractions.description: A 14th-century Sufi shrine and one of the most impressive examples of Multani tile-work architecture.

attractions.name: Multan Fort / Qasim Bagh
attractions.description: The remains of an ancient fort and surrounding park, home to several historic shrines and the old citadel walls.

attractions.name: Shrine of Bahauddin Zakariya
attractions.description: A revered Sufi shrine, one of the oldest and most significant in Multan, the 'City of Saints'.

attractions.name: Ghanta Ghar (Clock Tower) & Hussain Agahi Bazaar
attractions.description: A colonial-era clock tower surrounded by one of Multan's busiest traditional markets.

attractions.name: Multan Museum
attractions.description: A museum showcasing artifacts from Multan's long history, including Indus Valley and Islamic-era items.

weather_info.climate_type: Hot desert/semi-arid climate, one of the hottest cities in Pakistan
weather_info.avoid_months: May to July (extremely hot, frequently among the highest temperatures in the country, 45°C+)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Extremely hot and dry, often exceeding 45°C

travel_tips.tip: Use the Multan Ring Road / Bypass to avoid the congested inner city when traveling between the airport and Cantt areas.
Ride-hailing apps work well in Multan for reaching the fort, shrines, and food streets.
Stay well hydrated and avoid outdoor sightseeing during peak afternoon heat, especially between April and July.
Visit the shrines and Hussain Agahi Bazaar in the early evening, when the area is lively but temperatures have cooled.

history.founded: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in South Asia, dating back thousands of years
history.city_history: Known as the 'City of Saints' for its many Sufi shrines, Multan has been ruled by the Persians, Greeks (visited by Alexander the Great), Arabs, Ghaznavids, Mughals, and Sikhs. It was historically a major trade hub connecting South Asia to Central Asia and the Middle East.
history.province_history: Punjab, meaning 'land of five rivers', has one of the longest continuous histories in South Asia, home to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization (Harappa), later ruled by the Mauryas, Mughals, Sikh Empire, and the British before becoming part of Pakistan in 1947.
